paragraphs.source_en: In 1276 and 1277, Nikephoros of Epeiros and Ioannes of Thessaly, who held their titles despot and sebastokrator from Michael, convened local counter-​ Synods that excommunicated Michael, Bekkos, and the pope. They were then counter-​excommunicated by Bekkos, but the popes would not back Bekkos up in this even though Michael requested it, as Epeiros was an ally of Charles of Anjou, who was still waiting for the green light to pounce.72 Despite Michael’s persecution, Rome was receiving reports that he was insincere and the Union a farce.73 Charles was meanwhile building up his alliance. In 1278, the Principality of Achaea came fully under his control and he began sending delegates (baiuli) to govern it in his name.

However, in that year the royal fleet defeated the Latin pirate fleet of Euboia (Negroponte) and the adjacent islands at the battle of Demetrias in the Pagasetic Gulf. Those Latins made their living by raiding Roman territories.
